rows.basis: Tesla says FY2023 capex included 'continued investment in AI' and 'investing in autonomy and other artificial intelligence enabled training and products' alongside factories, cells and Superchargers. It gives no AI amount or share of the $8.899B total. The PP&E 'AI infrastructure' category is not used, because other@v1 forbids PP&E-category estimates.

Tesla stated 'AI infrastructure capex' of $1.0B in Q1 and $0.6B in Q2 2024, so at least $1.6B for the first half. It stated no Q3, Q4 or full-year AI figure, so no full-year amount is given. The MD&A says the $11.34B total was 'mainly for AI-related capital expenditures, global factory expansion and machinery', which describes the whole and is not the AI part. The PP&E 'AI infrastructure' category change is not used, per other@v1.

Tesla says the $8.53B total was 'mainly for global AI and operational infrastructure and factory expansion' (the whole, not the AI part). It also says it added 16k H200 GPUs to Cortex (67k H100 equivalents) and is building Cortex 2 in Texas. No AI amount or share is stated, and PP&E-category estimates are not allowed under other@v1.
In Q1 2024 Tesla said it 'will continue to increase our core AI infrastructure capacity'. The 10-K expected total capex above $11.00B for 2025, which is the company total, not an AI amount.

Tesla expects total capex above $20B in 2026 'driven by our AI initiatives', including compute infrastructure and data centers, alongside manufacturing lines, AI-enabled fleet assets and retail/service/charging. Per rule 3 that $20B is the whole, not the AI part. Tesla also plans to more than double onsite Texas compute (H100 equivalents) in H1 2026, but gives no AI dollar amount.
Tesla says the opex increase was driven by Cybertruck pre-production, AI and other R&D programs. No AI cost amount or share of the $8.769B total is given.

The MD&A says opex increases were 'primarily driven by additional costs year over year related to AI programs', and the Q2 release says 'largely driven by AI projects'. No AI cost amount or share of the $10.374B total is given.

R&D expense rose $1.87B (41%), 'primarily due to increases in costs related to AI and other programs' plus $500M more SBC. That is a year-over-year change across AI and other programs, not an AI cost amount, and no AI share of the $12.739B total is given.

There is no FY2026 capex value in the pack, so no actual row is made (rule 4). FY2026 statements are qualitative only.
There is no FY2026 opex value in the pack, so no actual row is made (rule 4). FY2026 statements say opex rose on 'AI and other R&D projects' without an amount.
